story_title: As an Attendee, I want to withdraw from an event I registered for so that my place can become available again where permitted

acceptance_criteria.text: A registered attendee can withdraw their registration.
The attendee can no longer be treated as an active registrant.
The event's available capacity is updated where applicable.
Relevant Event Organisers or Coordinators can see the updated registration information.

open_questions: RESOLVED 2026-10-15: written after the code (branch SPM-52-Withdraw-from-Event). Every label, message and page address in the cases is what the code shows, and the page tests for My Registrations, the 'Your registration' card and the Registration card render the screens with the cases' wording. Run 2026-10-16 in Chromium (Playwright following each case's steps against `npm run dev` and the shared database, re-running `npm run fixtures:spm52` where a case says to): all 10 passed. 'Log out and log in as' was done in a fresh browser session.

RESOLVED 2026-10-15: where Withdraw is. A 'Withdraw' button on each 'Registered' row of My Registrations (the 'My Registrations' sidebar link), and beside 'You registered on <date>.' in the 'Your registration' card on the event page (UI_DESIGN S-27 and S-06 both expected it with #20). Both ask first: 'Withdraw from <event title>?' with 'Your place is released and can be taken by someone else. To attend, you would have to register again, and the event may be full by then.', buttons 'Keep my place' and 'Withdraw'. Afterwards: 'You have withdrawn from <event title>.' (My Registrations) or 'You have withdrawn from this event.' (event page). The text promises nothing about the waiting list, which is SPM-66.

RESOLVED 2026-10-15: AC2 status. Withdrawing sets the registration to 'Withdrawn' (badge 'Withdrawn') and records when. The row is kept, not deleted, so My Registrations still lists it and the attendee can register again while registration is open (SPM-51 already reactivates a withdrawn row).

RESOLVED 2026-10-15: only a 'Registered' registration can be withdrawn. Leaving the waiting list is Join and Respond to Waiting List (SPM-66), so a 'Waiting list' row has no Withdraw; 'Attended' and 'Withdrawn' rows have nothing to give back. Out of scope, so no case: what happens to the freed place when there is a waiting list (SPM-66) and notifications (SPM-53).

RESOLVED 2026-10-15: AC5. The organiser and coordinators see two extra rows on the event's Registration card while registration is enabled: 'Places taken' ('3 of 10 · 7 left', or just the number when no capacity is set) and 'Withdrawn' (how many attendees have withdrawn). Places taken counts Registered and Attended, as SPM-51's capacity rule does. The full list of who registered is the Attendees tab (S-11), a separate story. Other roles (Ops Manager, Venue Staff, Technical Support, Safety Officer, Attendee) don't see the rows. Decided with the team on 2026-10-13.

OPEN: an attendee can withdraw at any time - after registration has closed, and even after the event's date while it is still Confirmed. The acceptance criteria set no cut-off. Should withdrawing stop at some point (e.g. when registration closes, or when the event starts)?

OPEN: the 'Places taken' and 'Withdrawn' rows only show while registration is enabled. When the coordinator turns registration off after attendees registered (as for 'SPM52 Members Gala'), the organiser and coordinator see 'Not enabled for this event' and no counts, so a later withdrawal is not visible to them. Should the counts show whenever the event has registrations?
OPEN: every coordinator who can see the event gets the counts, not only its assigned coordinator (the registration:view_list permission is per role). Is 'relevant coordinator' the assigned one only?

RESOLVED 2026-10-15: not reachable from the screens, so covered by route tests only (src/app/api/__tests__/registration-withdraw.test.ts): a non-attendee calling the withdraw API, withdrawing another attendee's registration (404, nothing changed), and a request asking for any status other than withdrawn.

RESOLVED 2026-10-15: fixtures. `npm run fixtures:spm52` (scripts/seed-spm52.ts) deletes and recreates only the six 'SPM52 …' events (seed keys spm52_*), with their registration settings and Marcus Yeo's registrations; the same events (without those) are at the end of prisma/seed.ts, and the base seed gives them no random registrations. No pinned reference numbers: find each event by title. The open events' registration runs to 31 Dec 2027, so the cases hold until then.
